data.claim: The interface census records every hard-coded URL host as a network dependence, so the Teams Adaptive Cards schema URL is a ratchet offender
data.falsifier: a schema-namespace URL literal is not counted as a network host
data.mechanism: archifaces_scan._literal_site matches any string literal to _URL and adds network host:<host>; notify_outbound.CARD_SCHEMA is the schema namespace
data.probe_output: pre-fix: FAILED - host:adaptivecards.io in the network census
data.question: Is adaptivecards.io a network dependence ddflow must track, or a format-identifier URL that should be excluded from the census?

chunk_findings.detail: The exclusion is keyed on the host, not on a schema identifier. Any string the existing URL census already matches whose host is `adaptivecards.io` is dropped, including a real endpoint. Given `url = "https://adaptivecards.io/v1/notify"` (or the same host with a path the project actually calls), `m.group(1).lower()` is `adaptivecards.io`, `not in _SCHEMA_HOSTS` is false, and `self.add("network", ...)` never runs. The census then reports no network dependence for a host the comment says belongs there whenever ddflow talks to it. The scanner only sees URL literals, so it cannot tell a `$schema` namespace from that call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:426

chunk_findings.detail: The new test’s docstring promises a hard-coded endpoint host such as `api.example.com` is still a network dependence, but the body only builds `http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json` and asserts that host is absent. A change that stopped recording every host (or inverted the filter) would still pass. The regression therefore does not lock the invariant the bug fix claims to keep.

chunk_findings.detail: The docstring and the scanner comment both promise that any non-schema path on adaptivecards.io is still a network site, but the body only excludes `http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json` and checks a different host (`api.example.com`). Given `v = "https://adaptivecards.io/v1/notify"` (or a filter that drops every URL whose host is adaptivecards.io), `v.lower().startswith(_SCHEMA_NS_PREFIXES)` is false only for the path-prefix check; a host-wide exclusion would still leave `host:adaptivecards.io` out of this scan and `host:api.example.com` in it, so both asserts pass and the regression does not lock the invariant the fix claims to keep.

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression asserts `len(f.sites) == 1` for `host:adaptivecards.io` after scanning one file that contains both `http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json` and `https://adaptivecards.io/v1/notify`. The baseline rows in this same change are one record per (kind, host, file) with an occurrence count in the fourth column (e.g. `host:[REDACTED:ipv4]` … `14`), and `add("network", f"host:{host}", …)` keys both strings to that same family and file. On unfixed code both URLs still collapse to a single site, so `len(f.sites) == 1` passes and the test never goes red; only a host-wide drop (zero sites) fails it. The assertion never reads the site count, so it does not lock B489298dd27.
